_comment: PROTOTYPE overrides. Intensity is derived from cost; this is the one override the design admits, and it exists to record where the author disagrees with an item's price. Kept here rather than in data/items.json while the model is still moving -- these graduate into meta.intensityGrade once the grades settle. A closed set of named grades on purpose: a free multiplier field would drift from cost exactly the way meta.potency already did.

intensityGrades.description: Costs what it's worth, and no more
Price says it all -- the default, never authored
Cheap to buy, potent to work with

_items_comment: Keyed by item name for legibility in a prototype. Seeded with the reagent class the map turned up on its own: full elemental saturation, near-zero cost. These are the 'cheap yet intense' case.
_disciplines_comment: Prototype stand-in for meta.disciplines. An item's discipline membership says which crafts can PRODUCE it -- not what it can be used as an ingredient for, which is ungated. Absent means the default: Weapon/Armor -> blacksmithing, Accessory -> tinkering, consumable with mp_heal -> cooking, other consumable -> alchemy, junk -> its existing craftKind. Only the interesting exceptions are written here, and overlap is the cheapest way to make a thin discipline feel furnished.
